blocks.text: Zscaler supports Basic authentication, a simple authentication scheme built into the HTML protocol. Basic authentication prompts users for a username and password, which are sent as a Base64 encoded string in the HTTP request header.
Basic authentication is not enabled by default. To access this feature, submit a support ticket from the Zscaler Admin Console.

blocks.heading: How Basic Authentication Works with Zscaler

blocks.text: The following diagram provides an overview of the Basic authentication flow with Zscaler:

blocks.item: The client sends a request along with the authentication credentials of its corresponding user enrolled with Zscaler.
A Public Service Edge for Internet & SaaS (ZIA) calculates the HA1 value for the given credentials and authenticates the user upon successful validation.
The traffic proceeds to its destination and a 200 OK verification code is sent back to the Zscaler service and client.

blocks.item: Basic authentication works with an HA1 value that must be initialized. Therefore, users need to be enrolled to the Zscaler Admin Console via API. This is necessary because Basic authentication is often used for workloads, which may not be able to interactively perform user enrollment on a browser.
For more information about user enrollment, see Deploying Basic Authentication.

After users are enrolled, they can browse the internet through an Internet & SaaS proxy and one of several forwarding proxy methods such as Static IP, DPCC, Virtual Service Edge for Internet & SaaS, or with transparent proxy such as GRE and VPN. User traffic from locations can be configured for Basic authentication and the desired forwarding method.
